text:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate across us-west-2 region. Error spike started ~ 1784004300. Summary: 5xx (segfault/502) and request timeouts. Paging maria (oncall).

maria (oncall): I'm on it. Looking at console metrics now — tailing the model-runner logs for GPU nodes.

jonah (eng-runtime): thx. I see a cluster of segfaults from runner-ml-23 and runner-ml-24. Kernel exit code 139 in the logs. Could be CUDA OOM or a kernel driver crash. Can you paste the logs? I'll check core dumps.

maria (oncall): pasting last 80 lines from runner-ml-23:

```
[2026-03-14T10:12:01Z] model_runner[pid:4217]: INFO start inference request batch_id=978
[2026-03-14T10:12:02Z] model_runner: WARNING kv_cache miss for prefix_id=12
[2026-03-14T10:12:02Z] model_runner: ERROR unexpected signal 11 (segfault) at 0x7fffb5c3
[2026-03-14T10:12:02Z] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID 4217, GPU 0
[2026-03-14T10:12:02Z] systemd: model-runner.service: main process exited, code=killed, status=11/SEGV
```

maria (oncall): multiple similar traces across runners. cpu/mem looks fine. GPU mem metrics show spikes then reset.

lee (eng-ml): Could be a bad quantized kernel path for the new 4-bit kernels under high sequence lengths. We rolled a micro-optimization yesterday that touched attention kernel handling. @jonah did we roll that runtime change to canaries?

jonah (eng-runtime): yes, we pushed runtime patch r-2026.03.13 to canary and then to prod yesterday. Can reproduce locally on a long sequence test with batch size 6 — gets CUDA Xid 13. I'm rolling back the kernel selection change on canary now.

anya (support): Customers impacted: three high-traffic customers showing 5xx increase; two reported degraded UX. I've opened a ticket for each and linked them to this thread. Need ETA for mitigation to communicate.

maria (oncall): Mitigation options: (1) immediate traffic reroute to fallback model variant (cpu-safe) for affected customers, (2) scale down concurrency / batch_size on the runners, (3) roll back runtime patch. Which is fastest? 

jonah (eng-runtime): quickest is route (1) + (2). Rolling back will take ~15-25m and a deploy restart -> potential flapping. I'll do (2) now: reduce global batch cap from 8->2 on prod runtime via flag. Command:

```
./ctl runtime set-config --batch-cap 2 --target=prod
```

jonah (eng-runtime): running command... ok returned 202 Accepted. Should propagate in ~30s.

maria (oncall): changing routing for the three customers to fallback variant now (canary to fallback-model:v1-safe). Doing via console -> per-customer routing. @anya can you confirm customer consent/notice text? I'll apply routing as emergency override.

anya (support): Sending message templates now. I'll notify customers A & B with workaround (failover model) and estimated partial impact. Customer C explicitly asked to stay on primary; pinging account team for permission to failover.

deploy-bot: rollouts: flag-change applied to 16/16 runtime nodes in prod. No failures reported.

maria (oncall): I'm seeing 5xx rate drop by ~60% in the last 2 min. Timeouts also trending down. Core dumps are being collected to S3: s3://redwood-core-dumps/1784004321/

jonah (eng-runtime): collecting a sample core and minimal repro. I'll run it under cuda-memcheck locally to check for invalid memory access. If it's the attention kernel, we should stop selecting that kernel path until a proper fix.

lee (eng-ml): I'll prepare a quick patch to disable the new kernel selection heuristics and open PR. If we push a runtime-config that disables that path we can avoid full rollback.

maria (oncall): good. Plan for next 30m: maintain reduced batch cap, keep routed customers on fallback unless account says no, collect cores, jonah + lee to push config to disable problematic kernel selection, then gradual re-enable if stable. Anyone object?

anya (support): fine. I'll update customer-facing incident note and set expectation ~1h until full mitigation.

jonah (eng-runtime): started a debug deploy to canary with kernel-selection disabled. Logs look clean so far for long-seq test. If no regressions in 10m we can push prod config change.

maria (oncall): handing off to jonah for active mitigation. I'm going offline in 20m for another paging rotation—@jonah you'll own incident until next handoff. I'll remain reachable.

jonah (eng-runtime): taking over on-call. I'll post updates here. Current status: 5xx down ~75%, fallback routing active for 2 customers, awaiting config rollout.

sre-bot: INCIDENT: status=investigating -> mitigating, incident_id=INC-20260314-1784, severity=high, linked_channel=#incidents

maria (oncall): ack. Thanks team. Keep me in the loop for customer C decision.

(End of thread)
